title: Replace the initiative-deep tenant byte scan with behavioural probes, then wire the directory whole

scope.judgedWhole: Every test file in the directory is a row, so the directory leaves the dark baseline whole rather than partial.
scope.everyFileWasExecuted: Each file was run on its own with npx jest --runTestsByPath <file> --no-coverage --ci on the branch: 3 of 3 green, 65 cases (4 + 7 + 54).

rewrite.removedCase: grep invariant — no hardcoded tenant key in src/lib/atlas/initiative-deep/
rewrite.whyRemoved: It asserted that six quoted spellings of three tenant keys were absent from the bytes of nine files. A key written any other way (a template literal, a concatenation) passed it with the behaviour unchanged, and a comment naming a key failed it with no behaviour at all.

addedCases.perCarrierFence: Every tenant-keyed read the view makes (engagement lookup behind gates.passed and gates.upcoming, the engagement-scoped and portfolio signal reads, tower_ai_tool_usage, tower_dora_metrics) is seeded for both tenants with a marker per carrier, and each carrier is asserted on its own for each caller: own marker present, other tenant's marker absent. The fixture carries hostile rows only a fence can exclude: an engagement in each tenant tagged with the other tenant's initiative id and listed first, and a signal in each tenant pointing at the other tenant's engagement. 12 cases.
addedCases.industryRead: The clients row read for the industry code is recorded and must be the caller's own id. 1 case.
addedCases.tenantKeyInvariance: For every key in CANONICAL_TENANT_KEYS and LEGACY_TENANT_ALIASES from src/lib/tenant/aliases.ts (36 distinct keys, read from code rather than typed), the same data under that key and under a neutral key must produce deep-equal views. This fails whether a key is special-cased or used as a literal filter, however it is spelled. The three keys the byte scan listed are all members of the legacy alias list (measured on the branch). 36 cases.

rewrite.unchanged: The five existing behavioural cases (two leak checks, two wrong-tenant-id nulls, the in-tenant percentile) are kept verbatim.

mutations.howRun: Each mutation was applied to one product file, the suite run, and the file restored with git checkout. The same eleven were run against the pre-change suite from origin/main.
list: M1 drop the client_id fence on tower_ai_tool_usage
M2 drop the client_id fence on tower_dora_metrics
M3 drop the client_id fence on the engagement lookup (gates.ts)
M4 drop the client_id fence on the engagement-scoped signal read
M5 drop the client_id fence on the portfolio signal backfill
M6 hard-code the clients.id filter to one tenant id
M7 special-case one tenant key with a quoted literal (return no tower samples)
M8 add a literal-key filter on the signal backfill
M9 drop the client_id fence on the portfolio-position read
M10 drop the client_id fence on the initiative row
M7b as M7, with the key written as a concatenation of two template literals
mutations.caughtByPreChangeSuite: 4 of 11 (M7, M8, M9, M10). M7b, the same behaviour as M7 spelled differently, passed the byte scan.
mutations.firstDraftFinding: The first draft of the per-carrier fixture caught 8 of 10: M3 and M4 survived because no cross-tenant row existed that only those fences excluded. The hostile engagement and stray signal rows were added for that reason, and both are caught now.

wiring.step: Run the T-782 atlas initiative-deep suites
wiring.namedAsADirectory: Named as a DIRECTORY without a trailing slash; it leaves product-directory-ci-coverage.baseline.json in the same change (123 -> 122 lines).

notInScope: src/lib/atlas/initiative-deep/joins/__tests__ is a separate dark directory and is not judged here. phase_approvals and engagement_phases are read by engagement_id only; their fence is the engagement lookup, which M3 now proves.

suites.rationale: Unchanged. Green, behavioural, reads no repository file. Held by T-781 only for its sibling's scanner case.
Unchanged. Green, behavioural, reads no repository file. Held by T-781 only for its sibling's scanner case.
